A prodigal son 'joins himself' to a citizen of a far country (Luke 15:15), Paul commands believers to 'cling to' what is good (Rom 12:9), and Jesus quotes Genesis to declare that a man shall 'be joined to' his wife (Matt 19:5). Even dust can kollaomai to sandals (Luke 10:11).     Enriched: To cling devotedly to an abstract moral good. In Romans 12:9 Paul exhorts believers to be 'clinging to the good' (kollōmenoi tō agathō). The metaphor of glue is preserved: moral goodness should stick to the believer as permanently as glue bonds surfaces.

  Sense 3: "be joined in marital union"
    Enriched: To be united in the bond of marriage, echoing the Genesis creation ordinance. Spanish 'se-unirá' and French 's'attacher' both underscore the permanent, covenantal adhesion that marriage entails — the strongest form of human bonding the verb can express.

    Enriched: To stick physically to a surface, as dust adhering to sandals. In Luke 10:11 the seventy-two are told to wipe off 'the dust having clung to' (kollēthenta) their feet.
